Simplest model: time = ~0.1 s fixed + steps x per-step cost. Per-step cost is pixel-proportional compute plus a large bandwidth-bound part on the 31x31 stem maps. Accuracy rises slowly with total steps, about 0.2 pp per 0.5 epoch, which is 1.5-2.7 s/pp. The E036 tip scored 5.31 s and 0.7532 on seeds 0-2. Fresh seeds 13-22 gave 0.7525, so the population mean is about 0.752-0.753, only 0.2-0.3 pp above the 0.75 bar. The tip sits at the accuracy cliff.

Mechanisms and evidence:
1. Early low resolution is cheap (E026, E033). E040 and E041 each saved 0.1-0.17 s but cost 0.07-0.2 pp. The 32 px tail and the 3x3 final-map regime carry accuracy (E011, E018, E024).
2. Backward truncation saves more time than its MAC share (E028, E034, E036). The dose is nonlinear: E037's 60% freeze cost about 0.4 pp. E042's partial freeze read 0.7549 at 5.27 s, which is noise-compatible with neutral. E039's BN fold is not worth it.
3. Averaging, LS, warmup and Lookahead-interval tweaks (E025, E029, E030, E032) are null or negative. The recipe is in a narrow local optimum, so shade non-systems changes by about -0.1 pp.
4. wd x0.5 helped about 0.2 pp (E016). Muon's gain is confounded with batch size and an RNG re-draw (E006).
5. Systems-only work is worth about 1-2% each. Math-identical changes keep per-seed outcomes bit-identical (E035).
6. Sample dropping (E031) costs about 0.3-0.4 pp for about 0.5 s, which is no better than the epoch dial.
7. Any change to the RNG stream or step count re-rolls seeds 0-2, with scatter SE about 0.12 pp. E043 was a no-change profiling run, yet it read 0.7497 against 0.7532 for the same commit. So either the harness is not bit-reproducible run to run, or the 3-seed noise is about 0.2 pp. I now treat 3-seed noise as about 0.15-0.2 pp.

Noise: time +/-0.03 s. 10-seed SE is about 0.06 pp. Seeds 3-12 carry a winner's curse of about 0.1-0.2 pp.

Misses: the times of E034, E037 and E041 (savings were larger than modelled), E037's accuracy cliff, E042's accuracy (better than predicted), and E043's accuracy drift on an identical recipe.

Unsure: the true tip mean; whether BN recalibration adds anything (it plausibly adds 0.05-0.2 pp, because the lerped BN stats are mismatched); whether bandwidth-bound levers transfer to the PCIe judge; and where the stem inefficiency lives.

forecasts.reason: BN recalibration may add a little, since lerped BN stats mismatch the averaged weights. Cost is 0.03-0.1 s, and the effect is small relative to noise.
Doubling steps in the 20 px phase adds launch overhead, so time rises by about 0.15 s. Accuracy gains maybe 0.1 pp, which is within noise.
Freezing group 2 saves about 1.5% of time. The tip is on the accuracy cliff, so a loss of 0.1-0.2 pp is likely.
This is a diagnostic with no recipe change. It will likely show a large non-GEMM share and a low-efficiency conv1, which is consistent with H6.
The E031 mechanism costs about 0.15 pp for about 0.1 s, which is no better than the dial. The tip is at the cliff.
Padding Cin from 24 to 32 plausibly speeds up conv1 by 1-3%. Math is identical, but fp16 summation order changes, so seed outcomes re-roll slightly.

cruxes: Is the harness bit-reproducible run to run? E043 reran the identical commit and read 0.7497 against 0.7532, so is the true 3-seed noise about 0.2 pp?
What is the true population mean of the E036 tip on 20+ unselected seeds? If it is below 0.752, nearly every further time cut is infeasible.
Does the profile show group-1 conv1 or the 31x31 stem maps taking more than 15% of step time? If so, padding the channels is worth doing.
